# Anthropic reported $16.8B in Q3 revenue — what the investor figures show


By OpenTools Team


·


October 15, 2026


Anthropic reportedly told prospective IPO investors that quarterly revenue reached $16.8 billion. The sequence shows fast growth and a clear slowdown, while profitability still needs public definitions.


##


Anthropic reportedly presented a $16.8 billion quarter to prospective investors


Anthropic's revenue reached $16.8 billion in the third quarter, according to an investor who attended a private pre-IPO meeting and spoke with[Reuters](https://www.reuters.com/business/finance/anthropics-q3-revenue-surges-45-nearly-17-billion-2026-10-14/) . Reuters reported the company had $4.7 billion of revenue in the first quarter and $11.6 billion in the second.[The Information](https://www.theinformation.com/briefings/anthropic-reports-16-8-billion-third-quarter-revenue) separately reported that Anthropic gave prospective IPO investors the $16.8 billion figure at a Wednesday presentation in San Francisco.


The disclosure is material because it describes actual quarterly revenue rather than a short-period annualized run rate. It is still a reported private-company presentation, not a public earnings release. Anthropic has not published the presentation, and the figures have not yet appeared in a public registration statement with audited notes.


That distinction should travel with every chart or comparison built from the numbers. The reporting supports the $16.8 billion top line and the quarter-to-quarter sequence; it does not provide a complete income statement, balance sheet, cash-flow statement or revenue-recognition policy.


##


The useful signal is a bigger business with slower sequential growth


The move from $11.6 billion in Q2 to $16.8 billion in Q3 is a 44.8% sequential increase and adds $5.2 billion of revenue. The previous move, from $4.7 billion in Q1 to $11.6 billion in Q2, was a 146.8% increase and added $6.9 billion. OpenTools calculated both rates directly from the quarterly figures reported by[Reuters](https://www.reuters.com/business/finance/anthropics-q3-revenue-surges-45-nearly-17-billion-2026-10-14/) .


Revenue therefore kept expanding quickly, while both the percentage growth rate and the absolute dollars added fell from the prior quarter.[Axios](https://www.axios.com/2026/10/15/anthropic-q3-revenue-cash-flow) also described the pace as slower than the jump between Q1 and Q2. Deceleration is normal as a base gets larger; the point is to avoid compressing two different claims into one headline. Anthropic reportedly grew by $5.2 billion in the quarter, but it did not preserve Q2's more-than-doubling pace.


[The Information](https://www.theinformation.com/briefings/anthropic-reports-16-8-billion-third-quarter-revenue) said Q3 revenue was more than 3.6 times Anthropic's revenue for all of 2025. That comparison captures the scale-up, though a single quarter and a full prior year are different periods and should not be presented as a like-for-like growth rate.


##


Quarterly revenue is not the same metric as annualized run-rate revenue


Multiplying the reported Q3 revenue by four produces a simple $67.2 billion annualized pace. That calculation is useful as a scale check, but it is not an official forecast and it should not automatically be labelled ARR. A quarter can include usage spikes, contract timing, credits, partner revenue and other effects that a month-end run-rate metric may handle differently.


Anthropic's own[May Series H announcement](https://www.anthropic.com/news/series-h) said its run-rate revenue had crossed $47 billion earlier that month. In August,[Axios reported](https://www.axios.com/2026/08/17/anthropic-revenue-run-rate-ipo-openai) more than $11.5 billion of preliminary Q2 revenue and an annualized run rate above $65 billion at the end of July. Axios explicitly cautioned that companies may not measure these figures the same way.


The reported $16.8 billion quarter is broadly compatible with a business operating around the high-$60-billion annualized scale. It does not prove a specific exit-rate figure, and it cannot be used to reconcile monthly run rate to recognized quarterly revenue without Anthropic's definitions.


##


The profitability claims need definitions before they can be compared


[The Information](https://www.theinformation.com/briefings/anthropic-reports-16-8-billion-third-quarter-revenue) reported an 11% adjusted operating margin for the year through Q3, not for Q3 alone, and said the measure excludes major costs including stock compensation.[Axios](https://www.axios.com/2026/10/15/anthropic-q3-revenue-cash-flow) reported that Anthropic described itself as cash-flow positive. Those are encouraging signals, but they answer different questions.


Adjusted operating margin depends on which expenses are removed. Cash-flow positive could refer to operating cash flow, free cash flow or another company-defined measure. Neither phrase, on its own, establishes GAAP net income, the economics of serving each model request or the cost of future training and infrastructure commitments.


The minimum responsible reading is narrow: the company reportedly told prospective investors that the business is generating positive cash under its chosen measure and showed a positive adjusted operating margin for the year to date. The public reporting does not supply the reconciliation needed to test those measures against stock compensation, capital spending, working-capital movements or long-term compute obligations.


##


A public filing must connect growth to durable unit economics


Anthropic[announced in June](https://www.anthropic.com/news/confidential-draft-s1-sec) that it had confidentially submitted a draft S-1 to the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission. Because that draft is not public, investors and customers cannot yet inspect the accounting policies and risk factors that would make the revenue presentation comparable with a listed company.


The public document should answer at least five questions: how usage and committed contracts are recognized as revenue; gross margin after inference and cloud costs; customer and product concentration, especially Claude Code; the bridge from adjusted operating margin to GAAP results; and the timing and cancellation terms of compute and infrastructure commitments. It should also reconcile cash flow to capital expenditure and disclose material stock-based compensation.


Until then, the reported quarter is strong evidence of rapid commercial adoption, not a complete verdict on the economics of frontier AI. Follow Anthropic's products and related reporting on the[Anthropic organization page](https://opentools.ai/organizations/anthropic) .
